DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** Christ had no biological father among men. Joseph was supposed to be his father and stood in that place by law and by naming. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost," and the human nature came from Mary alone. [L4, built below]

## 1. Mary conceived as a virgin, with no union with a man

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The Greek συνελθεῖν (synelthein, "to come together") marks the marriage union. The conception is placed *before* it.

**[L1] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." **[L2]** παρθένος (parthenos, "virgin").

**[L1] Luke 1:34:** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** The verb is γινώσκω (ginōskō, "know"), here of marital knowledge.

**[L3] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." **[L2]** The same verb stands here (ἐγίνωσκεν, eginōsken, "knew").

**[L4]** Mary says she knows no man (Luke 1:34). Matthew says Joseph "knew her not" through the birth (Matthew 1:25). Both use ginōskō in one sense. So no man, Joseph included, had known her when the child was conceived.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** γεννηθὲν (gennēthen) is the passive of γεννάω (gennaō, "beget/conceive"). ἐκ (ek) means "out of, from" and names the source.

**[L3] Matthew 1:2:** "Abraham begat Isaac." The same root gennaō is used of fathers throughout the genealogy. In Matthew 1:20 it is applied to what is in Mary, and the "out of" is *the Holy Ghost*, not a man.

**[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** ἐπισκιάσει (episkiasei, "will overshadow") is used for the power of God coming upon her. The child is τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον ("the holy thing being born"), which is "of thee," of Mary.
- **[L2]** The Greek διὸ καί (dio kai, "therefore also") ties the title "Son of God" to this very conception.

**[L4]** Luke 1:35 names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the agent, and "of thee" as the human source. Matthew 1:20 gives the origin as ek pneumatos hagiou ("out of the Holy Ghost"). The text names no human male source, so there is no room for a biological father among men.

## 3. Joseph is "supposed" father, not begetter

**[L1] Luke 3:23:** "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** ἐνομίζετο (enomizeto, "was thought/reckoned") speaks of what people supposed, not of what was so.

**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** The Greek is ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη (ex hēs egennēthē, "out of whom was born"). The relative ἧς (hēs, "whom") is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone.
- **[L3] Matthew 1:2–15:** the pattern "X begat Y" is repeated. It breaks at verse 16, where the verb is passive and the antecedent is feminine.

**[L1] Matthew 1:19:** "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, ... was minded to put her away privily."
**[L3] Matthew 1:20:** "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

**[L4]** Joseph's reaction to the pregnancy (Matthew 1:19) and the angel's correction of it (Matthew 1:20) show he knew he was not the source. By taking Mary and naming the child (**[L3] Matthew 1:21, 25:** "thou shalt call his name JESUS"; "he called his name JESUS"), he became the legal father.

**[L1] Luke 2:48:** "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
**[L1] Luke 2:49:** "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?"
**[L4]** Mary speaks of Joseph as father by common usage. The child answers with a different Father, in Luke 2:49. Both verses stand together in one scene.

## 4. Prophecy foretold a woman-only conception

**[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
- **[L2]** The Hebrew word is עַלְמָה ('almah), which stands behind the KJV's "virgin."
- **[L3] Genesis 24:43:** "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." The same word is used of Rebekah, whom **[L3] Genesis 24:16** describes as "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
- **[L3] Isaiah 7:11:** "Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God." A sign is set as something beyond the ordinary course.

**[L1] Matthew 1:23:** "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." Matthew applies the prophecy to this birth, and uses parthenos.

**[L3] Jeremiah 31:22:** "the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man."

**[L4]** A sign (Isaiah 7:11) fulfilled in a virgin (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:23) is a conception without a man's part. Jeremiah's "new thing" fits this.

## 5. The Son was sent into the world, not begotten into it by a man

**[L1] Galatians 4:4:** "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."
**[L1] Hebrews 10:5:** "a body hast thou prepared me."
**[L1] John 6:38:** "I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me."

**[L4]** The Son is the one *sent*, so he was there before the "body" was prepared (Hebrews 10:5). This is a supporting point only: the origin of the conception is already carried by Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35.

**[L1] John 6:42:** "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"
**[L4]** This is the opinion of the crowd. It matches Luke 3:23, "as was supposed," and is not the Gospel's own account of the birth.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Mary conceived as a virgin, before any union with Joseph or any man: [L1] Matthew 1:18, Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:25 + [L2] ginōskō ("know") in Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25 + [L2] synelthein ("to come together") in Matthew 1:18.
2. The source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man: [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 + [L2] ek ("out of") and episkiasei ("overshadow") + [L3] Matthew 1:2, where the same root gennaō is used of fathers.
3. Joseph is father only by supposition and by law: [L1] Luke 3:23, Matthew 1:16 + [L2] enomizeto ("was supposed") and hēs ("of whom," feminine) + [L3] Matthew 1:21, 25 (naming) and Luke 2:48–49.
4. Scripture foretold a woman-only conception as a sign: [L1] Isaiah 7:14 + [L2] 'almah ("virgin," as the KJV renders it) + [L3] Genesis 24:16, 24:43, Isaiah 7:11, Jeremiah 31:22 and Matthew 1:23.
5. The human body came from Mary through God's preparing, and the Son was sent, not begotten by a man: [L1] Hebrews 10:5, Galatians 4:4 + [L3] John 6:38 + [L4] chain from "sent" and "prepared" to a conception with no human male source.
6. Therefore Christ had no biological father among men; he was conceived of the Holy Ghost, and Joseph was his supposed and legal father only: [L4] resting on links 1–5, specifically Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and Luke 3:23.

# Defender, Round 2 (re-issued with the six flagged sentences replaced)

I answer the question first. Then I take C1–C4 and each press in turn, quoting the pressed verses. I rest the case on Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, and I carry those against each press.

---

## 1. Answer to the question: how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda?

**[L1] Hebrews 7:14:** "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- **[L2]** The verb is anatellō (G393, "to rise, spring up"). It speaks of descent and rising, and gennaō (G1080, "to beget") is a different verb. The evidence is prodēlon (G4271, "plainly evident"), a public matter. Numbers 1:18 sets a public reckoning of this kind.

**[L1] Numbers 1:18:** "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- **[L2]** The words are bayith (H1004, "house, family") and 'ab (H1, "father"). The reckoning is by house.

**The house of the fathers my rows name is Joseph's.**
- **[L1] Luke 2:4:** "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L1] Luke 2:5:** "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:21 and 1:25:** "thou shalt call his name JESUS" and "he called his name JESUS."
- **[L1] Luke 3:23:** "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** hōs (G5613, "as") with enomizeto (G3543, "was reckoned, supposed") marks the reckoning of the public. The sentence sets Joseph's sonship inside the bracket "as was supposed," so the verse reports what was thought.

**Reckoning by "the house of their fathers" is a reckoning by law, and it can stand where another man is the begetter.**
- **[L3] Deuteronomy 25:6:** "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother." The child is counted in the house of the dead brother, and a different man is the begetter.
- **[L3] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The pattern of "begat" runs through Matthew 1:2–15. At Joseph the sentence changes to "the husband of Mary, of whom was born."
- **[L4]** Numbers 1:18 (house of the fathers) and Deuteronomy 25:6 (a child counted in a house whose father did not beget him) show that a pedigree by the father's house can rest on law. So Luke 2:4–5 and Matthew 1:21, 25 place the child in the house of David by Joseph's reckoning, and Hebrews 7:14's "evident" rests on that public reckoning.

**The seed of David is also stated through the woman.**
- **[L1] Galatians 4:4:** "made of a woman."
- **[L1] Romans 1:3:** "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- **[L2]** Both verses use ginomai (G1096, "to become, be made"). The woman and the seed of David stand in one construction.
- **[L4]** Galatians 4:4 applies ginomai to the woman, and Romans 1:3 applies it to David's seed. So the flesh "of the seed of David" is the flesh "made of a woman." That agrees with Luke 1:35, "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

---

## 2. The challenger's chain, C1–C4

**C1. "Fruit of his loins" names descent at any remove.**
- **[L1] Acts 2:30:** "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ."
- **[L2]** osphys (G3751, "loins").
- **[L3] Hebrews 7:10:** "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Levi, generations later, is in the loins of Abraham. **[L3] Hebrews 7:5:** "come out of the loins of Abraham."
- **[L4]** In Acts 2:30, Hebrews 7:5 and Hebrews 7:10 the loins carry descent at any remove. So Acts 2:30 and 2 Samuel 7:12 ("proceed out of thy bowels") require David's line, and that line is what Hebrews 7:5 and 7:10 describe, a line of descent that spans generations. C1 itself says "in David's line."

**C2. "Joseph, thou son of David" names Joseph's lineage. The same sentence names the source of what is in Mary.**
- **[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin reads "conceived: Gr. begotten." That is the challenger's own margin.
- **[L2]** gennēthen is the passive of gennaō (G1080, "to procreate, beget"). It is the same root as "begat" in **[L3] Matthew 1:2**. The preposition ek ("out of") gives the source: the Holy Ghost (pneuma hagion, G4151/G40).
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:2 uses gennaō for the fathers' begetting. Matthew 1:20 uses the same root for what is in Mary and gives its source as the Holy Ghost. So the begetting spoken of in Matthew 1:20 is the Holy Ghost's, and Joseph is the man addressed in the same sentence.
- **[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise." The Greek houtōs (G3779, "in this manner") announces that the birth came about in the way set out by what follows. What follows is "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**C4. The sequence the rows give places the conception before the union.**
- **[L1] Luke 1:34:** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:24:** "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife."
- **[L4]** The rows run in this order. Mary knows no man (Luke 1:34). The Holy Ghost comes upon her (Luke 1:35). She is found with child "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18). Only afterward does Joseph take his wife (Matthew 1:24). The challenger needs a union between Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:18, and Matthew 1:18's "before they came together" is the stated place where that union would fall. The conception is placed ahead of it.

---

## 3. Answers to the presses

### Press on D1 (Luke 1:31, Matthew 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7)
The press MEANS that Mary conceived by Joseph after the angel spoke and before the taking, so that the "till" of Matthew 1:25 begins only at the taking.

- **[L1] Luke 1:31:** "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The future tense says the conception is still to come when the angel speaks. Mary's question in Luke 1:34, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?", is tied to that conception.
- **[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." This is the answer given to her "how," and it supplies the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the means of the very conception Luke 1:31 announces.
- **[L4]** Luke 1:31 announces the conception, Luke 1:34 asks how, and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost coming and the power overshadowing. So the conception of Luke 1:31 is the conception whose cause Luke 1:35 gives, and that cause is the Holy Ghost with the power of the Highest, in answer to "seeing I know not a man."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." This is said before the taking of Matthew 1:24. By Matthew 1:20 the conception is already past ("is conceived"), and the angel reassures Joseph about the source before he takes her.
- **[L3] Deuteronomy 20:7:** "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" The verse marks betrothal and taking as two steps. Matthew 1:18 sets the coming together after the finding: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." So the coming together that Deuteronomy 20:7's taking would bring lies after the conception.

### Press on D2 (1 John 5:1, John 1:13, Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, Luke 1:32)

**1. "Born of God" in believers (1 John 5:1, John 1:13).**
- **[L1] John 1:13:** "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." The birth "of God" is set against "of blood" and "of the will of man."
- **[L3] John 3:6:** "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." **[L3] John 3:4:** "Can he enter the second time into his mother's womb, and be born?" The second birth is not a womb-conception.
- **[L4]** The believer has two births: from a father in the womb, and "of God." The believers' parallel therefore concerns a second birth added to the first. Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 speak of the one conception in Mary: "that which is conceived in her," "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

**2. The verbs of Luke 1:35 in Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34.**
- **[L2]** eperchomai (G1904, "come upon") and episkiazō (G1982, "overshadow") carry their sense from their context. In Acts 1:8 the context is "ye shall receive power... ye shall be witnesses." In Luke 9:34 the context is a cloud. In Luke 1:35 the context is the answer to a question about conceiving: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L4]** The same verbs mean power coming in each place. In Luke 1:35 that power answers the "how" of a conception and is named as the cause of the holy thing "born of thee." So I take the verb with its own context, as the challenger does with theirs.

**3. dio kai ("therefore also") and Luke 1:32.**
- **[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** dio (a conclusion word, "wherefore, therefore") stands inside verse 35. It draws its conclusion from the clauses placed immediately before it in the same verse: the Holy Ghost coming and the power of the Highest overshadowing.
- **[L4]** Luke 1:32 gives the title. Luke 1:35 states the reason for the title: "therefore."

**4. 2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6 (Solomon, two fathers).**
- **[L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6:** "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." Solomon's sonship to God rests on the words "I have chosen him."
- **[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The sonship here rests on "therefore also," a conclusion drawn from the Holy Ghost coming and the power overshadowing, with the child "born of thee."
- **[L4]** Solomon is "thy son" to David and "my son" by God's choice. In Matthew 1:20 the source of the conception is given as the Holy Ghost. So the Solomon pattern is a choice upon a man who has a begetter, while Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 name the Holy Ghost as the cause of the conception itself.

**5. Psalm 2:7 and Acts 13:33.**
- **[L1] Acts 13:33:** "in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee."
- **[L4]** Acts 13:33 attaches the psalm's "begotten" to the raising. That is a separate matter from the conception in Mary. The conception is the subject of Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, so the psalm stands beside their statement that the conception is "of the Holy Ghost."

### Press on D3 (Luke 2:48, Luke 2:27, 1 Chronicles 28:6)

**Matthew 1:19, the meaning of the press.** The press asks how Joseph's reaction shows he knew he was not the source.
- **[L1] Matthew 1:19:** "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The angel's word is phobēthēs (from phobeō, G5399, "to be afraid"). The fear is about taking her.
- **[L4]** The angel meets Joseph's fear with the source of the conception ("for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"). The "for" gives the reason the fear is groundless. A man who knew himself the source would have no fear for the angel's reason to remove. So the text carries Joseph's mind: he was minded to put her away because he did not know himself the source.

**Luke 2:48 and Luke 2:27.**
- **[L1] Luke 2:48:** "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L1] Luke 2:27:** "when the parents brought in the child Jesus."
- **[L2]** goneis (G1118, "parents") names those in a parent's place.
- **[L1] Luke 3:23:** "(as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L1] Luke 2:49:** "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- **[L1] Luke 2:51:** "and was subject unto them."
- **[L4]** Luke 3:23 puts the common usage under "as was supposed." Luke 2:48 is that usage, and Luke 2:49 is the reply "my Father's." Luke 2:51, "was subject unto them," states that he obeyed those in the parents' place. The begetting is carried by Matthew 1:20, "of the Holy Ghost."

**enomizeto and Acts 16:13.**
- **[L1] Acts 16:13:** "where prayer was wont to be made."
- **[L2]** G3543 in both is the verb of deeming. In Acts 16:13 it is a place deemed one of prayer. In Luke 3:23 it follows hōs ("as") and is bracketed in the KJV. Both are reckoned facts.

**hēs and Genesis 4:25.**
- **[L1] Genesis 4:25:** "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son." The father's act is named: "knew."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Matthew uses that same verb of knowing about Joseph, with the negative.
- **[L4]** Genesis 4:25 states the father's knowing. Matthew 1:25 states the same verb with the negative through the birth. So the contrast sits in Matthew's own words.

### Press on D4 (Isaiah 7:14, Isaiah 8:3, Proverbs 30:19, Jeremiah 31:22)

**'almah and bethulah.**
- **[L1] Genesis 24:16:** "a virgin, neither had any man known her." **[L1] Genesis 24:43:** "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]."
- **[L2]** Genesis 24:16 uses bethulah (H1330, "virgin"). Genesis 24:43 uses 'almah (H5959). Both verses are about Rebekah.
- **[L4]** The KJV renders 'almah "virgin" of the very woman Genesis 24:16 says no man had known. So Isaiah 7:14's "virgin" is a fair rendering of the word. In Exodus 2:8 ("the maid") and Proverbs 30:19 ("a maid") the word names an unmarried maid.

**Isaiah 8:3 and Isaiah 7:16.**
- **[L1] Isaiah 8:3:** "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." The margin reads "approached."
- **[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** the child's name is "Immanuel."
- **[L4]** The child of 8:3 is named Mahershalalhashbaz by command. The child of 7:14 is named Immanuel. They are two children with two names, so 8:3 records another conception beside the sign of 7:14.
- **[L1] Isaiah 7:11:** "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above."
- **[L4]** A sign in "the depth" or "the height above" lies beyond the ordinary run of things. The conception of 8:3, by a man's approach, is an ordinary one.

**Matthew 1:22–23.**
- **[L1] Matthew 1:22:** "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying."
- **[L1] Matthew 1:23:** "Behold, a virgin shall be with child."
- **[L4]** "All this" in 1:22 takes in the whole of 1:18–21, including "of the Holy Ghost" (1:18, 1:20). The fulfilment is therefore a virgin with child before any coming together.

**Luke 1:27 ("espoused to a man").**
- **[L1] Luke 1:27:** "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
- **[L2]** The espousal is mnēsteuō (G3423, "to betroth"), a promise. Matthew 1:18 places the coming together after the conception. I grant she was an espoused wife (Matthew 1:20).

**Jeremiah 31:22.** I hold this as a supporting text.
- **[L1] Jeremiah 31:22:** "the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man."
- **[L2]** bara' (H1254, "to create") marks a new thing, and an ordinary conception is no new thing. My case rests on Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and Isaiah 7:14, with Jeremiah beside them.

### Press on D5 (Galatians 4:4, Matthew 11:11, John 1:6, Hebrews 2:14–17)
I grant that "born of women" is said of John (Matthew 11:11) and that "sent" is said of John (John 1:6). D5 is a supporting link, and my case rests on Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35.
- **[L1] Hebrews 10:5:** "a body hast thou prepared me." The one who prepares is "thou," God.
- **[L1] Hebrews 2:14:** "he also himself likewise took part of the same." **[L1] Hebrews 2:16:** "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham."
- **[L4]** Hebrews 2:14 and 2:16 state that he took part of flesh and blood and took on the seed of Abraham. Galatians 4:4 and Romans 1:3 give the source of that flesh: "made of a woman" and "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." So the flesh he took is the flesh made of the woman, and in it the seed of David.

### Press on D6 (Luke 1:27, Luke 1:36, Luke 1:5, Romans 1:3)
- **[L1] Luke 1:36:** "thy cousin Elisabeth." **[L1] Luke 1:5:** "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron."
- **[L2]** "cousin" here renders syngenis (G4773, "a kinswoman"). It states a kinship between Mary and Elisabeth.
- **[L4]** The point of Mary's descent stands on Galatians 4:4 and Romans 1:3 (the same ginomai with ek for the woman and for the seed of David). It also stands on Luke 1:32, where the angel tells Mary that "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

---

## 4. Two presses of my own on the challenger's keystone

**Press on C2/C5. A pedigree by the house of the fathers is a reckoning by law.**
- **[L1] Numbers 1:18** ("by the house of their fathers") and **[L3] Deuteronomy 25:6** ("shall succeed in the name of his brother") show a child counted in a house while another man is the begetter.
- **[L4]** C5 needs "named in the house of David by Joseph" to mean "begotten by Joseph." Deuteronomy 25:6 shows a house-reckoning that stands on law. So C2 does not carry C5.

**Press on C4. It is bounded inside its own sequence.**
